incident_spec.summary: Slow SELECT query on sys.databases with OBJECT_ID checks and filtering.
symptoms: Query execution takes 9-21 seconds on a local dev machine with 4 databases.
incident_spec.mechanism: Potential blocking due to long-running transactions or inefficiencies in OBJECT_ID function evaluation.

facts.evidence: The query uses OBJECT_ID to check for the existence of a specific table in each database.

facts.key: Execution plan shows clustered index seeks.
facts.evidence: The DBA mentions clustered index seeks taking up 22%, 24%, and 48% of the execution plan.

facts.key: Query performance improved with WHERE clause.
facts.evidence: Adding the WHERE clause reduced execution time from 21 seconds to 9 seconds.
The DBA explicitly states they have no control over the indexes of the databases.

assumptions: The issue is caused by blocking due to long-running transactions or inefficiencies in OBJECT_ID evaluation.
The query is executed on a SQL Server-compatible environment.
unknowns: Whether the issue is reproducible in the target environment.
The exact database schema and data distribution in the target environment.
